fable.w: The tempting reading is that an "Interdepartmental" committee of cabinet officials reporting to Congress is purely intra-governmental coordination. That fails because the Committee must include at least 14 non-Federal public members (patients, family members, clinicians, advocates, judges, law enforcement) and is subject to the Federal Advisory Committee Act. Those outside members help produce specific recommendations for actions federal agencies can take, so outsiders are brought into federal decisionmaking through an advisory committee.
fable.s: The Committee shall also include not less than 14 non-Federal public members appointed by the Secretary of Health and Human Services

opus.w: The section sets up an advisory committee under the Federal Advisory Committee Act. At least 14 of its members must come from outside the federal government, including patients, family members, advocacy groups and professionals. The committee gives federal agencies specific recommendations on coordinating mental health services. The reports to Congress and the federal members do not change the answer, because the outside members bring people from outside the government into federal policy advice.
opus.s:
(2) Non-federal members.—The Committee shall also include not less than 14 non-Federal public members appointed by the Secretary of Health and Human Services, of which—
            (A) at least 2 members shall be an individual who has received treatment for a diagnosis of a serious mental illness;
opus.b: The obvious misreading is to call this "No" because the Committee's main output is a report to Congress, and Congress is inside the federal government. It also looks like coordination between federal agencies only. That reading fails because the Committee is an advisory committee covered by the Federal Advisory Committee Act. By law, it must include at least 14 non-federal public members, such as people who have been treated for serious mental illness, family members, advocacy organizations, clinicians and judges. It also gives agencies recommendations on how to coordinate mental health services. An advisory panel with outside members meets the definition.

qwen_chat.w: The committee is explicitly composed of both federal and non-federal members, and the non-federal members are appointed to serve on the committee, which is a form of participation. It looks like participation because it involves a committee that includes non-federal members.
qwen_chat.s: (2) Non-federal members.—The Committee shall also include not less than 14 non-Federal public members appointed by the Secretary of Health and Human Services, of which— (A) at least 2 members shall be an individual who has received treatment for a diagnosis of a serious mental illness; (B) at least 1 member shall be a parent or legal guardian of an adult with a history of a serious mental illness or a child with a history of a serious emotional disturbance; (C) at least 1 member shall be a representative of a leading research, advocacy, or service organization for adults with a serious mental illness;
qwen_chat.b:
Temptation: It looks like participation because it involves a committee that includes non-federal members.
Resolution: The committee is explicitly composed of both federal and non-federal members, and the non-federal members are appointed to serve on the committee, which is a form of participation.
